To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Wechseler subtest scores are significantly related to 6 of the neuropsychological conditions; (b) only 6 of 84 correlations were consistent across samples; (c) the correlations were not significant for the 4 other neuropsychological conditions.
the relationships between Wechsler test performance and neuropsychological diagnoses are weak and inconsistent across samples of children.

the Wechsler test is a useful tool in the assessment of the neuropsychological status of children with learning disabilities, but the results of this research suggest that it is not a sensitive enough tool for use in the diagnosis of minimal brain dysfunction or hyperkinesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between Wechsler test performance and neuropsychological functioning,
the relationship of children's WISC and WISC- R test scores to 6 neuropsycho-logical conditions in two samples.
the neuropsychological significance of the Wechsler intelligence test.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Wechsler Intelligence Test scores have little or no value in the differential diagnosis of neurobehavioral dysfunction in children with average intelligence. (Author/DB)
the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Revised (WISC-R) is not a valid instrument for the neuropsychological assessment of children.
the Wechsler test battery is useful for the assessment of children's cognitive abilities but not for the assessment of specific neurobehavioral conditions in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WISC-R is not a useful tool for the diagnosis of specific neuropsychological conditions.
the Wechsler tests have limited diagnostic significance for children with average intelligence.

(a) the Wechsley subtest scores are not sufficiently sensitive and specific to have diagnostic significance in children of average intelligence, and (b) the neuropsychological conditions of minimal brain dysfunction and hyperkinesis are not sufficiently defined to be related meaningfully to cognitive functioning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WISC-R is not an effective tool in the diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders.
the WISC and WISC–R are not sufficiently sensitive measures to be used as diagnostic instruments.
the Wechsler test is not sensitive to neuro-psychological dysfunction in children of average intelligence.
